name: The Harbor Table
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. Ur's excavated game boards come from the Royal Cemetery (c. 2600-2400 BCE); the tavern itself is game fiction.

name: The Ziggurat Steps
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. The game was played across the Near East for two millennia; every tavern character here is fiction.

name: The Wool Merchant
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. The long-route ruleset is a modern reconstruction, not attested at Ur.

name: The Wharf Bench
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern with invented house rules: no safe rosettes, and any roll past the end bears off.

name: The Scribe's Court
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. The Tablet ruleset follows BM 33333B (177-176 BCE): five pieces and astragal dice are attested there; the rest is filled in.

name: The Guard's Post
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. Boards like the British Museum's Ur board are the visual model; Theben game finds are not attested.

name: The Merchant Quarter
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. The Senet-like variant is Kendall's reconstruction, one of several; no Senet rules are attested.

name: The Priest's Table
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. Gammon here doubles a shut-out loss; the rule is borrowed from backgammon (Invented).

name: The Market Stall
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. Patolli is known from Duran's 16th-century account; the exact board used here is reconstructed.

name: The Canal Canoe
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. Duran reports Patolli played for stakes; the wager layer shown here is game fiction.

name: The Featherworker
label: invented
historyNote: Invented tavern. The long-route ruleset is a modern reconstruction used as the circuit's hard table.

name: The Eagle Table
label: invented
historyNote: Invented final tavern. All stakes are in-game purse only; no real money is involved anywhere in the game.
